requirements.text: Make her close her jacket fully

outcomes.description: The woman's jacket is closed completely.
outcomes.target: The jacket is fully closed, with its front panels brought together and no visible opening remaining along the closure.
outcomes.reference: The woman's jacket in the input image.

nodes.question: Comparing the same jacket's front closure in the source and edited images, is there reliable visual evidence that the closure progressed toward being closed?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if corresponding visible features show the front panels brought closer together or a greater portion of the closure joined in the edit. Fail only if comparable visible evidence establishes no progress or movement away from closure. Unknown if pose, viewpoint, occlusion, or visibility prevents a reliable comparison; an open-looking edited jacket alone does not establish failure.
nodes.binding: Compare the woman's same jacket and identifiable front-panel or closure features across source and edit. Assess change only; do not judge whether the edited jacket is fully closed. Preserve uncertainty when the images do not permit a reliable like-for-like comparison.

nodes.question: In the edited image, is there a visible opening between the jacket's front panels along the closure, rather than only a panel flaring outward with the woman's turned pose?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the front panels visibly meet along the entire closure with no opening remaining. Fail if a visible gap between the panels remains along the closure. Unknown if the closure is obscured or the pose, occlusion, or fabric movement makes it impossible to distinguish a closure gap from a panel flaring outward.
nodes.binding: Inspect only the woman's jacket in the edited image. Judge the front closure itself, not the silhouette or a panel's outward position. Use the ancestor's endpoint observation as context, but independently assess whether the apparent opening is actually along the closure.

nodes.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed, with no visible opening remaining along its closure?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the jacket's front panels meet along the entire closure and no opening remains. Fail if any visible opening remains along the closure. Unknown if the closure is obscured or the image does not provide enough evidence to determine whether it is fully closed.
nodes.binding: Assess the same jacket and closure as in s1. Full closure is the requested endpoint; partial closure is not complete fulfillment.

nodes.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed?
nodes.criteria: Complete only if s1 passes, s2 passes, and s3 passes: comparative progress is established and the edited jacket is fully closed. Partial if s1 passes and either s2 or s3 fails, establishing progress but not full closure. Absent only if s1 fails with reliable comparative evidence establishing no progress, regardless of endpoint appearance. Unknown if s1 is unknown, or if s1 passes but endpoint evidence from s2 or s3 is unresolved. Do not infer progress from endpoint appearance or treat an uncertain endpoint as incomplete.
nodes.binding: Target: The jacket is fully closed, with its front panels brought together and no visible opening remaining along the closure.. Reference: The woman's jacket in the input image..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The fulfillment rule is contradictory and does not faithfully compose the support evidence. It requires s3 to pass for completion, but s3 passes when the panels meet with no opening—the same endpoint condition as s2 passing—and fails when a gap remains. Yet the rule calls s1 pass plus either s2 or s3 fail partial, so a fully closed jacket with s2 pass and s3 fail would be labeled partial, while a gap could also be treated as partial based on either failure. The separate s2 and s3 endpoint checks overlap, and the composition does not resolve their conflicting or redundant results. Use one endpoint check, or define a non-overlapping composition that treats full closure as complete and evidenced progress with an open closure as partial."}

parsed.reason: The fulfillment rule is contradictory and does not faithfully compose the support evidence. It requires s3 to pass for completion, but s3 passes when the panels meet with no opening—the same endpoint condition as s2 passing—and fails when a gap remains. Yet the rule calls s1 pass plus either s2 or s3 fail partial, so a fully closed jacket with s2 pass and s3 fail would be labeled partial, while a gap could also be treated as partial based on either failure. The separate s2 and s3 endpoint checks overlap, and the composition does not resolve their conflicting or redundant results. Use one endpoint check, or define a non-overlapping composition that treats full closure as complete and evidenced progress with an open closure as partial.
